chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from al-Husayn and al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ayman ibn Muhriz, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

None of our Shias gets up for prayer except that he is surrounded by angels equal to the number of his opponents, and they pray behind him, supplicating to Allah, the Mighty and the Sublime, for him until he finishes his prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for a Shia when performing prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* underscores the concept of *al-muqabalah* (counterbalance), where angels equal in number to the believer's opponents intercede for him, symbolizing divine validation of the Shia community amidst opposition. It highlights the spiritual protection and communal solidarity inherent in the act of prayer, reinforcing the status of the faithful as those who are actively supported by the celestial realm during their worship.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan from al-Hussain and al-Hassan b. Aban from al-Hussain b. Sa’eed from Ayman b. Muhriz from Muhammad b. al-Fudhayl from Abi Hamzah from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

None of our Shias gets up for prayer except that he is surrounded by angels equal to the number of enemies around him and they pray behind him and supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and the Sublime for him till he finishes his prayer.”
